name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield rose above 5.3% on 13 Nov, highest since late October, as bets on a December rate rise grew
state: The 10-year gilt yield fell towards 5.1% on 6 Nov, its lowest since late August, then rose above 5.3% on 13 Nov, its highest since late October, after Q3 GDP growth of 0.7% and LSEG data putting the chance of a December Bank Rate rise above 80% (Trading Economics). The two-year yield rose above 5%, its highest since October 2023. The move is inside the 40bp monthly line, but yields remain elevated after the Bank of England's 5 Nov rate rise, so Watch is kept.
for_you: Higher gilt yields tend to feed through to fixed mortgage pricing and government borrowing costs over the following weeks. The Bank of England publishes its rate decisions and Monetary Policy Reports; its next decision is scheduled for December.
rubric_hit: 10y move under 40bp in a month; Watch kept on elevated yields after BoE's 5 Nov hike (hysteresis)

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK gilt yields (11–13 Nov updates)
Morningstar (Dow Jones) — Sterling rises, gilt yields trim losses after BOE raises rates

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
